answer: An island mapping market could ask agents to mark a grove in nadir-facing drone images. Each accepted map earns a payment that vests only after randomly scheduled field checks; the agent must leave a portion as a dispute reserve, and high-value jobs require several cleared maps. A swarm of new identities must obtain fresh images, survive separate checks, and tie up many reserves before it can earn much. Wealthy operators can still bankroll many accounts, while bad field checks may penalize honest workers.
